topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by framing the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Core Principles and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the fundamental architecture of the complement cascade, explaining its general functions, nomenclature conventions, and the central mechanism of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the three distinct recognition routes—alternative, lectin, and classical—that initiate the complement cascade and converge on surface C3 convertase deposition.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the primary downstream immunological outcomes of complement activation: opsonization, inflammation recruitment, and direct membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the surface and soluble regulatory proteins that protect host tissues from accidental complement attack by inactivating convertases and blocking pore formation.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how genetic and acquired deficiencies in specific complement components lead to distinct clinical pathologies, from recurrent bacterial infections to autoimmune manifestations.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement Defenses
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture session and previews the subsequent topic on the adaptive immune system.
